sources.lw2008: Leyse-Wallace, Linking Nutrition to Mental Health (iUniverse, 2008)

facts.text: Aim for enough sleep to wake up without an alarm. Too little raises the risk of obesity, depression, high blood pressure, weakened immunity and anxiety.
Sleep apnea can look exactly like ADHD. Waking up tired is worth getting checked.
Sleep hygiene basics: screens off an hour before bed, phone charging outside the bedroom, and a dark, cool room.
Coffee 30–60 minutes before bed delays sleep and worsens its quality. Much of caffeine's felt boost is just reversing overnight withdrawal.
The brain runs on steady glucose. Mixed meals (carbohydrate + protein + fat) every 3–5 hours, breakfast included, keep it steady. Some people do best with six smaller meals 2.5–3.5 hours apart.
Eating enough carbohydrate and fat spares protein for growth and repair, rather than burning it for fuel.
Baseline adult protein needs are about 0.8 g per kg of body weight. Egg white and milk are the highest-quality proteins.

In the Minnesota semi-starvation study, volunteers on ~1,600 kcal/day grew irritable, apathetic and preoccupied with food. Recovery tracked calorie intake: those refed more generously recovered faster.
The food–mood link runs both ways: nutrients build and run the brain, and mental state changes what and how much a person eats.
Healthy ways to raise dopamine: exercise, creativity, and connection to people or a bigger goal.
Exercise raises dopamine and norepinephrine much like stimulant medication does, so a burst of activity sharpens focus for a while afterward.
Exercise releases BDNF, a protein the authors call "Miracle-Gro for the brain."
A 2018 review (700+ people, 8 countries) found 20–30 minutes of moderate exercise improved reaction speed and precision. 65% improved at planning and organizing after a single session.
People with ADHD often have a different sense of time, with only two settings: "now" and "not now."
The ADHD brain is a Ferrari engine with bicycle brakes: powerful and fast, with weak brakes. Structure and routine are how you strengthen the brakes.
